body.translated_text: <s>Kādambarīsvīkaraṇasūtramañjarī</s> (A Garland of Sūtras on the Acceptance of Kādambarī Liquor)
In a sacrifice (<s>saptatantu</s>) not produced by another, the acceptance of <s>anutarṣa</s> (the thirst-quencher, i.e. <s>kādambarī</s> liquor) is absolutely necessary. // 1

children.text: * idānīm ātmabhuvā kriyamāṇe saptatantau tatsādhanatvenānirvacanīyasukhodbodhahetutvena vāruṇīprāśanam anudarśayati ananyajasaptatantāv iti || 1.1
children.translated_text: * Now, in the sacrifice being performed by the Self-born (<s>Ātmabhū</s>, i.e. <s>Kāmadeva</s>), [the author] demonstrates the drinking of <s>Vāruṇī</s> (liquor of <s>Varuṇa</s>) as the means for that [sacrifice], because it causes the awakening of indescribable bliss — [this is conveyed by the words] 'in a sacrifice not produced by another.' // 1.1

children.text: * anutṛṣyanti anirvacanīyānandaṃ prāpnuvanti anenety anutarṣaṃ kādambaraṃ tasya svīkaraṇam anuprāśanaṃ tasya prāśanasyātyāvaśyakatvam atīva īpsitatamatvam anirvacanīyānandapradātṛtvena retaḥstambhakatvena hetunā karmānuṣṭhānāt pūrvaṃ pracetasaḥ kanyāyāḥ svīkaraṇaṃ kartavyam ity arthaḥ || 1.2
children.translated_text: * '<s>Anutarṣa</s>' means that by which they obtain (<s>anutṛṣyanti</s>) indescribable bliss; [this refers to] <s>kādambara</s> (liquor); its 'acceptance' (<s>svīkaraṇa</s>) means its drinking; the 'absolute necessity' of that drinking means it is most supremely desired, because it bestows indescribable bliss and because it causes the stiffening of the seed (<s>retaḥstambhaka</s>). The meaning is: prior to the performance of the rite, the acceptance of the daughter of <s>Pracetas</s> (<s>Varuṇa</s>) — i.e. liquor — must be accomplished. // 1.2

children.text: * makaradhvaja ātmabhūḥ ity amaraḥ || 1.3
children.translated_text: * '<s>Makaradhvaja</s> (the banner-of-the-crocodile, i.e. <s>Kāmadeva</s>) is [called] <s>Ātmabhū</s> (the Self-born)' — so says the <s>Amarakośa</s>. // 1.3

children.text: * saptatantur makhaḥ kratur ity amaraḥ || 1.4
children.translated_text: * '<s>Saptatantu</s> (seven-threaded) means <s>makha</s> (sacrifice), <s>kratu</s> (rite)' — so says the <s>Amarakośa</s>. // 1.4

children.text: * nanu anutarṣasvīkaraṇam adṛṣṭaphalodbodhe upakārakam āho svit dṛṣṭaphalodbodhe upakārakaṃ veti saṃśayavākyam upanyasya dṛṣṭaphalodbodhe eva sākṣād upakārakaṃ na kiṃcit svargādiphalavat ānuśravikavākyaṃ kalpyam upakārakam iti manasi niścitya pūrvasūtrasya hetutvena dvitīyaṃ sūtram anuśāsti || 1.5]
children.translated_text: * Now, a statement of doubt is presented: is the acceptance of <s>anutarṣa</s> beneficial for the awakening of unseen results, or is it beneficial for the awakening of seen results? Having determined in the mind that it is directly beneficial only for the awakening of seen results — and that no scriptural statement (<s>ānuśravikavākya</s>) postulating [unseen] results such as heaven, etc. need be devised as the cause — [the author] teaches the second sūtra as the reason for the first. // 1.5]

body.translated_text: * [Commentary on the <s>Kādambarīsvīkaraṇasūtramañjarī</s>:
Because [<s>kādambarī</s>] is the cause of the awakening of the bliss of love-play (<s>rati</s>), which is an indescribable bliss. // 2

children.text: * ratyānandasyeti || 2.1
children.translated_text: * 'Of the bliss of love-play' — // 2.1

children.text: * anutarṣasvīkaraṇe kṛte satīti jñeyam || 2.2
children.translated_text: * It should be understood: 'when the acceptance of <s>anutarṣa</s> has been performed.' // 2.2

children.text: * anena vākyena anayoḥ kāryakāraṇasaṃgatiḥ upapāditā bhavati tathā cāyam arthaḥ anutarṣasvīkaraṇe kṛte sati nidhuvanavyāpāre ratyānando 'nirvacanīya utpadyate netarathā sāmudrikaṇāmiśritasya sūpaśākādidravyasyeva nīrasaḥ svāduḥ prādurbhūyate ity arthaḥ || 2.3
children.translated_text: * By this statement, the relationship of cause and effect between these two is established. And the meaning is this: when the acceptance of <s>anutarṣa</s> has been performed, in the activity of love-making (<s>nidhuvanavyāpāra</s>), the bliss of <s>rati</s> (erotic pleasure) arises as indescribable — not otherwise. [Without it], like a broth of vegetables and such things not mixed with <s>sāmudrikaṇa</s> (sea-salt), [the experience] becomes tasteless — this is the meaning. // 2.3

children.text: * anyad apy anirvacanīyam upakārāntaraṃ tṛtīyasūtreṇa anuśāsti saṃpradarśayati || 2.4]
children.translated_text: * [The author] teaches — i.e. demonstrates — yet another indescribable benefit by means of the third sūtra. // 2.4]

body.translated_text: * [Commentary on the <s>Kādambarīsvīkaraṇasūtramañjarī</s>:
In the arousal of the <s>udañji</s> (phallus), the acceptance of the daughter of <s>Pracetas</s> (<s>Varuṇa</s>) is the supreme cause. // 3

children.text: * udañjyabhyutthāne iti || 3.1
children.translated_text: * 'In the arousal of the <s>udañji</s>' — // 3.1

children.text: * pāśinaḥ ātmajāyayā saha atiprītyupacayena tādātmyabhāvaṃ gamite sati nimittakāraṇasyātyupakārakatayā taddvārā svakīyānandasyānirvacanīyāhlāde prayojakībhūtaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ || 3.2
children.translated_text: * The meaning is: when one has attained a state of identity with one's own wife through an excess of affection for the Noose-bearer (<s>Pāśin</s>, i.e. <s>Varuṇa</s>), the instrumental cause becomes supremely beneficial, and through that, it becomes the efficient cause (<s>prayojakībhūta</s>) of the indescribable delight of one's own bliss. // 3.2

children.text: * anena vākyenātyāvaśyakatayā tādṛgvyāpārasya purastāt tādṛṅnirveśanaṃ sampādya tatpurastāt saptatantoḥ karmādhikāre 'dhikāritā itarathā nimittakāraṇe utsāhaśaktibhraṃśāt sākalyena narmavyāpāradhvaṃso bhavatīty arthaḥ || 3.3
children.translated_text: * The meaning of this statement is: with absolute necessity, such a preparation should be accomplished before such activity, and prior to that [the rite of] the sacrifice is authorized; otherwise, due to the loss of the power of enthusiasm in the instrumental cause, the amorous activity is entirely destroyed. // 3.3

children.text: * etasya sūtrasya rāddhāntasūtraṃ darśayati || 3.4]
children.translated_text: * [The author] now shows the established conclusion (<s>rāddhānta</s>) sūtra for this [teaching]. // 3.4]

body.translated_text: * [Commentary on the <s>Kādambarīsvīkaraṇasūtramañjarī</s>:
Because, in the absence of the principal agent of the one to be employed, it is impossible to perform the technique of love (<s>ratitantra</s>). // 4

children.text: * prayojyaprādhānye iti || 4.1
children.translated_text: * 'Of the principal agency of the one to be employed' — // 4.1

children.text: * prayojyasyodañjeḥ prādhānyakartṛtvam abhyutthāne sati sampadyate tadabhāve abhyutthānābhāve nimittāpāye naimittikasyāpy apāya iti nyāyena ratitantraṃ lupyate kutaḥ || 4.2
children.translated_text: * The principal agency of the one to be employed — the <s>udañji</s> (phallus) — is accomplished when there is arousal; in its absence — i.e. in the absence of arousal — by the principle that 'when the instrumental cause is absent, its effect too is absent,' the technique of love is lost. Why? // 4.2

children.text: * nimittakāraṇasyābhāvāt yathā turīvemādisattve paṭakāryasyotpattir netarathā tathā abhyutthānasattve tantravidhānasyotpattiḥ || 4.3
children.translated_text: * Because of the absence of the instrumental cause. Just as, in the presence of thread, shuttle, and so forth, a cloth is produced, but not otherwise — so in the presence of arousal, the performance of the technique is produced. // 4.3

children.text: * anena vākyenātyāvaśyakatvenānutarṣasvīkaraṇaṃ sampādya tatpurastāt nidhuvanavyāpāre pravṛttir vidheyā iti bhāvaḥ || 4.4
children.translated_text: * The purport of this statement is: having accomplished the acceptance of <s>anutarṣa</s> with absolute necessity, the engagement in amorous activity should be undertaken prior to that [i.e. before the excitement wanes]. // 4.4

children.text: * idānīṃ sūtracatuṣṭayasya sākalyena kṛtsnaṃ tātparyārthaṃ saṃgṛhya avyabhicaritaṃ sarvasūtrāṇāṃ rāddhāntavākyaṃ saṃpradarśayati || 4.5]
children.translated_text: * Now, [the author] gathers the complete intended meaning of the four sūtras as a whole and demonstrates the invariable established-conclusion statement of all the sūtras. // 4.5]

body.translated_text: * [Commentary on the <s>Kādambarīsvīkaraṇasūtramañjarī</s>:

body.text: prayojye narmavyāpāravistāre abhyutthānaviśiṣṭodañjyabhāve sarvāṅgīṇavyāpāropalakṣitaṃ ratitantraṃ kartum adhikārābhāvāt // 5
body.translated_text: When the one to be employed is engaged in the full extent of amorous activity, in the absence of an <s>udañji</s> distinguished by arousal, there is no authority to perform the technique of love characterized by the activity of all limbs. // 5

children.text: * prayojye narmavyāpāravistāre iti || 5.1
children.translated_text: * 'When the one to be employed is engaged in the full extent of amorous activity' — // 5.1

children.text: * pūrvasmin sūtre vāhyatantre yat kiṃcid avacchedenādhikārikatvaṃ nirūpitam asmin sūtre tu prayojakasya sākalyena narmapravṛttinimittasyābhāve jāyamāne sati prayojyavyāpāre 'pi atyantābhāvasya vidhānaṃ nirvyavasāyenaiva prāptaṃ bhavati kiṃcid viśeṣavidhānaṃ yatra nopalabhyata iti bhāvaḥ || 5.2
children.translated_text: * In the previous sūtra, a partial authority with some qualification was established regarding the external technique. But in this sūtra, when the complete absence of the cause for the employer's amorous engagement arises, even in the activity of the one to be employed, the absolute absence is established by inference alone — no additional specific prescription is found here; this is the purport. // 5.2

children.text: * tasmād anutarṣasvīkaraṇād anantaram eva narmakarmādhikāre ādhikārikatvam iti pañcasūtrāṇām eka eva tātparyārthaḥ || 5.3
children.translated_text: * Therefore, the single intended meaning of the five sūtras is this: authorization for the rite of amorous activity [comes] immediately after the acceptance of <s>anutarṣa</s>. // 5.3

children.text: * māghakirātaraghuvaṃśeṣu siddhāntitasya vākyasyaivāyam anuvādaḥ na tv apūrvavidhānaṃ svamanīṣayā upakalpya proktam iti śaṅkanīyam || 5.4
children.translated_text: * This is merely a restatement of what has been established in the <s>Māgha</s> [<s>Śiśupālavadha</s>], the <s>Kirātārjunīya</s>, and the <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> — it should not be suspected that this is a novel injunction fabricated by one's own intellect. // 5.4

children.text: * kiṃ ca dvitīyāvasthām atikrāntasya diṣṭyātmajāyayā saha asaṃstutapremaprāduṣkaraṇe saṃyuktasya janasya saprakārakarasotpattyanubhave tādṛṅmanīṣāyā abhāvāt sīdhusaṃgrahaṇaṃ paramakāraṇatvena nābhimatam taditarāvasthāyāṃ tu andhasaḥ śamalasya anirvacanīyānandaprakāśane svīkaraṇatvena saṃgrahaṇam atyāvaśyakatvenābhimatam eva īdṛksaṃvidā yāthārthyajñānaṃ parikalpya tādṛkkarmādhikāre anutarṣasvīkaraṇam atyāvaśyakatamam iti narmavyāpārakartṇām āptavākyavat yathārthopadeśam anuśāsti || 5.5]
children.translated_text: * Moreover, for one who has passed beyond the second stage [of life], and who, by good fortune, is united with his own wife in the manifestation of unacquainted love, the experience of the arising of a particular type of sentiment — for such a person, since such [youthful] disposition is absent, the collection of <s>sīdhu</s> (liquor) is not considered the supreme cause. But in the other stage [i.e., for one still in youth], the collection of <s>andhas</s> (liquor), being impure, is considered absolutely necessary for the manifestation of indescribable bliss, as the means of acceptance. Having determined the knowledge of truth by such understanding, [the author] teaches — as an authoritative instruction to those engaged in amorous activity — that the acceptance of <s>anutarṣa</s> is absolutely most necessary in such a rite. // 5.5]

body.translated_text: * [Commentary on the <s>Kādambarīsvīkaraṇasūtramañjarī</s>:
In the delight of the technique of love, in the arising of indescribable <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic flavor), the collection of <s>sīdhu</s> (liquor) is the supreme cause. // 6

children.text: * ratitantravilāse iti || 6.1
children.translated_text: * 'In the delight of the technique of love' — // 6.1

children.text: * ratitantravilāse narmavyāpāravilāse anirvacanīyarasotpattau ṣaḍvidharasād atirikto yo rasaḥ amṛtāndhasām upabhogayogya iti yāvat kādambararasasya anuprāśanasya paramakāraṇatvam tādṛgrase sampīte sati nidhuvanavyāpāravistāre rasabhāvanāviśeṣacaturāṇām anirvacanīyasukhodbodhaṃ janayatīty arthaḥ || 6.2
children.translated_text: * In the delight of the technique of love — that is, in the delight of amorous activity — in the arising of indescribable <s>rasa</s>: a <s>rasa</s> that exceeds the six [standard] <s>rasas</s>, one that is worthy of being enjoyed by the immortals and their food — this much is meant. The supreme causal nature of the <s>kādambara</s> (liquor) <s>rasa</s>, i.e. of its drinking: when such a <s>rasa</s> has been drunk, it produces the awakening of indescribable bliss in the full extent of amorous activity for those who are skilled in the cultivation of the particular <s>rasa</s> — this is the meaning. // 6.2

children.text: * kiṃ cānyad apy anirvacanīyaṃ rasaviśeṣāntaraṃ sīdhuprāśanenānudarśayati || 6.3]
children.translated_text: * Moreover, [the author] demonstrates yet another indescribable special <s>rasa</s> [produced] by the drinking of <s>sīdhu</s>. // 6.3]

body.translated_text: * [Commentary on the <s>Kādambarīsvīkaraṇasūtramañjarī</s>:
In the delight of the display of graceful amorous gestures and bonds, the innate nature of the wife of the Lord of <s>Puṣkara</s> (the West, i.e. <s>Varuṇa</s>) [is manifest]. // 7

children.text: * lalitavibhramabandheti || 7.1
children.translated_text: * 'In the display of graceful amorous gestures and bonds' — // 7.1

children.text: * puṣkaraṃ sarvatomukham ity amaraḥ || 7.2
children.translated_text: * '<s>Puṣkara</s> means all-faced (omnipresent)' — so says the <s>Amarakośa</s>. // 7.2

children.text: * puṣkarādhipateḥ ātmajāyāḥ lalitavibhramabandhaprāduṣkaraṇaṃ naisargikaḥ svabhāva iti sūtrārthaḥ || 7.3
children.translated_text: * The meaning of the sūtra is: the manifestation of graceful amorous gestures and bonds is the innate nature of the wife of the Lord of <s>Puṣkara</s>. // 7.3

children.text: * atra puṣkarādhipatiśabdena pratīcyāḥ kāṣṭhāyāḥ adhipatir lakṣyate tasya ātmajāyāḥ vāruṇyā anuprāśane kriyamāṇe lalitavibhramabandhānāṃ prakaṭīkaraṇe prayojikā bhavati netarathā kṛtsnavāṅmayasyādhidaivikarūpatvāt nirvyavasāyenaiva antaḥkaraṇasyāhlādakāḥ rucikaraprabandhāḥ atalapradeśāt kamalaniḥsaraṇam iva prāśanakartur mukhapadmanīḍāt prādurbhūyanta ity arthaḥ || 7.4
children.translated_text: * Here, by the word 'Lord of <s>Puṣkara</s>,' the lord of the western quarter is indicated — i.e. <s>Varuṇa</s>. When the drinking of <s>Vāruṇī</s>, his wife's [creation, i.e. liquor], is being performed, she becomes the efficient cause for the manifestation of graceful amorous gestures and bonds — not otherwise. Because the entire realm of speech has a supra-mundane (<s>adhidaivika</s>) form, by inference alone, compositions that delight the inner faculty and are charming emerge from the lotus-abode of the mouth of the drinker, just as a lotus emerges from the subterranean region — this is the meaning. // 7.4

children.text: * idam eva rasaviśeṣāntaraṃ saṃnipatyopakārakanyāyena paramāpūrvasādhane prayojakībhūtaṃ kāraṇaṃ nirbandhavarṇānāṃ śravaṇamātreṇa taddvārā manasijodbodhe anirvacanīyasādhanatvena paramakāraṇatvam ayam eva tasyāḥ naisargikasvabhāva iti || 7.5
children.translated_text: * This very special <s>rasa</s>, by the principle of 'combined contributory causes,' becomes the efficient cause in the supreme unprecedented accomplishment. Through it, merely by hearing the syllables of the bond [of verse], via that [channel], in the awakening of <s>Manasija</s> (<s>Kāmadeva</s>), its being an indescribable means makes it the supreme cause. This is her innate nature. // 7.5

children.text: * anyad apy upakārāntaram uttarasūtreṇa saṃpradarśayati || 7.6]
children.translated_text: * [The author] demonstrates yet another benefit by means of the next sūtra. // 7.6]

body.translated_text: * [Commentary on the <s>Kādambarīsvīkaraṇasūtramañjarī</s>:
With a woman approaching [the state of] dark complexion (<s>upaśyāmā</s>), the round of honey-drinking (<s>madhuvāra</s>) is the cause of extreme firmness of the <s>udañji</s> (phallus). // 8

children.text: * upaśyāmayeti || 8.1
children.translated_text: * 'With <s>upaśyāmā</s>' — // 8.1

children.text: * śyāmāvasthāyā upa samīpe vartate sā upaśyāmā tayā caturdaśapañcadaśahāyanātmikayā yoṣayā saha madhuvārā madhupānāvṛttiḥ udañjidhārṣṭye atyantadṛḍhataratve prayojako bhavati anena vākyena parisaṃkhyāvidheḥ svarūpaṃ prakāśitaṃ bhavati || 8.2
children.translated_text: * One who is near (<s>upa</s>) the dark state (<s>śyāmā</s>) is <s>upaśyāmā</s> — with such a young woman of fourteen or fifteen years; the round of honey-drinking (<s>madhuvāra</s>) means the occasion of drinking honey-liquor (<s>madhu</s>); it is the cause of extreme, exceedingly firm steadfastness of the <s>udañji</s>. By this statement, the form of the restrictive injunction (<s>parisaṃkhyāvidhi</s>) is made clear. // 8.2

children.text: * tathā cāyam arthaḥ atikrāntāvasthayā saha madhuvāre jāyamāne udañjidhārṣṭyaṃ naivotpadyate tayā saha tādṛgvyavasāyaḥ vaiyarthyatāṃ pratipadyate nyubjaghaṭopari jalapūraṇanyāyena tasmāt ratitantravilāse udañjidhārṣṭye manīṣāvatā puruṣeṇa galitayauvanayā saha madhuvāro naiva kartavya ity arthaḥ || 8.3
children.translated_text: * The meaning is thus: when the season of love arises with one whose youth has passed, boldness of the male organ does not arise; such resolve with her proves futile, like the maxim of pouring water over an inverted pot. Therefore, in the play of the erotic art, a wise man should never engage in the season of love with one whose youth has faded — this is the meaning. || 8.3

children.text: * nirarthakaprayāse kasyāpi matir naivotpadyata iti nyāyāt || 8.4
children.translated_text: * By the maxim that no one's mind inclines toward a fruitless endeavor. || 8.4

children.text: * dhanvantaryādīnāṃ matam anusṛtya kāpiśāyanasvīkaraṇe 'nirvacanīyāhlādadyotakam upakārāntaram anudarśayati || 8.5]
children.translated_text: * Following the opinion of <s>Dhanvantari</s> and others, [the author] shows an additional benefit in the consumption of <s>kāpiśāyana</s> (wine), which manifests indescribable delight. || 8.5]

body.translated_text: * [Commentary on the <s>Kādambarīsvīkaraṇasūtramañjarī</s>:
Intercourse with a <s>śyāmā</s> (a maiden of sixteen years) is the supreme cause of the retention of virility for the duration marked by two <s>yāmas</s> (six hours). // 9

children.text: * śyāmayā saheti || 9.1
children.translated_text: * 'With a <s>śyāmā</s>' — || 9.1

children.text: * ṣoḍaśavārṣikī śyāmeti vātsyāyanasūtre prasiddhiḥ tādṛgavasthayā yoṣayā saha niveśanaṃ pānaṃ patiṣu nirviviśur madam aṅganā ity atra nirveśanaśabde pānaṃ lakṣyate yāmapramāṇaṃ yāmadvayasaṃ pramāṇe dvayasaj iti sūtreṇa pramāṇārthe dvayasacpratyayaḥ tādṛkpramāṇopalakṣite diṣṭe kāle kālo diṣṭopyanehāpīti kośasmaraṇāt tāvat kālam abhivyāpyeti yāvat retaḥstambhane paramakāraṇam iti tayā saha kāpiśāyanasya svīkaraṇe kriyamāṇe ekayāmaparyantaṃ varāṅgopari vrīhikaṇḍanavat āghātaṃ karotīty arthaḥ || 9.2
children.translated_text: * A sixteen-year-old girl is well known as a '<s>śyāmā</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> of <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. 'Intercourse' (<s>nirveśana</s>) — i.e., drinking — with a woman of such age; as in 'the women indulged in intoxication with their husbands,' where the word <s>nirveśana</s> denotes drinking. '<s>Yāma</s>-measured' — by the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>dvayasaj</s> in the sense of measure,' the suffix <s>dvayasac</s> is applied in the sense of measure; '[for a duration] characterized by such a measure,' i.e., the appointed time — since the lexicon records '<s>kāla</s>' as also meaning 'appointed time' — 'pervading that much time,' this is the meaning. children.translated_text: * This restriction — that the observance applies on both days — is only for worshippers of <s>Śakti</s>. For other people, followers of the doctrine of the slayer of <s>Pralamba</s> [i.e., <s>Balarāma</s>], instruction is according to the [appropriate] time; the meaning is that there is no numerical limitation to [just] two days. || 27.2
* Moreover: || 27.3]

body.translated_text: * [<Commentary on the <s>Kādambarīsvīkaraṇasūtramañjarī</s>>
For the second <s>varṇa</s> [<s>kṣatriyas</s>], the permission is for all times. // 28

children.text: * dvitīyavarṇe iti || 28.1
children.translated_text: * 'For the second <s>varṇa</s>' — || 28.1

children.text: * kṣatrajātau dvitīyavarṇe kāpiśāyanasvīkaraṇavidhānaṃ sārvakālikaṃ tāmasīprakṛteḥ upāsanādhikāravatāṃ nirantaraṃ kādambarasvīkaraṇaṃ kartavyatvenābhimatam || 28.2
children.translated_text: * For those of the warrior-born second <s>varṇa</s>, the injunction for accepting <s>kāpiśāyana</s> (liquor) is for all times; for those of <s>tāmasī</s> (dark) nature who have eligibility for worship, the constant acceptance of <s>kādambara</s> (liquor) is considered obligatory. || 28.2

children.text: * aparokṣānubhavena tatsvarūpānudarśane upādānakāraṇatvāt ātmabhuvaḥ tanoḥ upāsanādhikāravat na ghasrayoḥ anuvartanam || 28.3
children.translated_text: * Because it is the material cause for the direct realization of its true nature through immediate experience, the eligibility for worship is like that of the body of the Self-born [<s>Brahmā</s>] — it is not limited to [specific] days. || 28.3

children.text: * aupadeśikavarṇasya niyamavidhānaṃ vidadhāti || 28.4]
children.translated_text: * He lays down the restrictive rule for the instructed <s>varṇa</s>: || 28.4]

body.translated_text: * [<Commentary on the <s>Kādambarīsvīkaraṇasūtramañjarī</s>>
For the first <s>varṇa</s> [<s>brāhmaṇas</s>], the permission is according to scriptural instruction, for the purpose of sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>). // 29

children.text: * yāgahetuneti || 29.1
children.translated_text: * 'For the purpose of sacrifice' — || 29.1

children.text: * vājapeye surāgrahān gṛhṇāti sautrāmaṇyāṃ surāgrahān gṛhṇātīti vākyadvayena prathamavarṇikasya yathāvācanikam eva grahaṇaprāśaneṣu ādhikāriko vidhiḥ || 29.2
children.translated_text: * By the two statements 'In the <s>Vājapeya</s>, one takes the cups of <s>surā</s>' and 'In the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>, one takes the cups of <s>surā</s>,' the authoritative injunction for the first-<s>varṇa</s> person regarding taking and drinking is strictly according to scriptural instruction. || 29.2

children.text: * tathā cāyam arthaḥ vājapeye tu grahaṇamātrasyaivābhyanujñānaṃ prāśanābhyanujñānaṃ tu tṛtīyavarṇasyaiva tathā cānuśravikavākyaṃ vimāthaṃ kurvate vājasṛta iti || 29.3
children.translated_text: * And thus the meaning: In the <s>Vājapeya</s>, only the taking [of the cup] is permitted; the permission for drinking, however, belongs only to the third <s>varṇa</s>. And the traditional statement is: 'The <s>vājasṛts</s> perform the churning (<s>vimatha</s>).' || 29.3

children.text: * sautrāmaṇyāṃ tu yāgakartur eva prāśanaṃ nigamavākyenābhidhīyate netareṣām ṛtvijām tatrāpy āghrāṇenaiva prāśanapratipattir iti matāntaram iti ṛṣyantarāṇāṃ vacanam iti || 29.4
children.translated_text: * In the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>, however, drinking is prescribed by Vedic statement only for the performer of the sacrifice himself, not for the other <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests). And even there, the understanding of 'drinking' is merely through smelling — this is an alternative opinion, the statement of other sages. || 29.4

children.text: * sārvakālikābhyanujñānaṃ tu rasādhipatīnām eva nānyeṣāṃ janānām iti prakaraṇārtham upasaṃharati || 29.5]
children.translated_text: * He concludes the section [by saying] that the permission for all times belongs only to the lords of tastes/pleasures, not to other people. || 29.5]

body.translated_text: * [<Commentary on the <s>Kādambarīsvīkaraṇasūtramañjarī</s>>

body.text: khaṇḍamaṇḍalādhipatyādīnām indirāvatāṃ janānām api sīdhugrahaṇasya vilāsaḥ sārvakālikaḥ // 30
body.translated_text: Even for people possessing <s>Indirā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>/wealth) who have lordship over small territories and other domains, the indulgence in taking <s>sīdhu</s> (liquor) is for all times. // 30

children.text: * khaṇḍamaṇḍalādhipatyādīnām iti || 30.1
children.translated_text: * 'Of those with lordship over small territories and other [domains]' — || 30.1

children.text: * alpaviṣayasya śāsanakartṇāṃ rājñāṃ lokamātur anugraheṇa paripūritānāṃ sīdhugrahaṇena vilāsānubhavaḥ vilāsānām anubhavanaṃ sārvakālikam na surathavaiśyādīnāṃ matam anusṛtya pravartanam ity arthaḥ || 30.2
children.translated_text: * For kings who govern small domains, who are graced by the Mother of the World [<s>Lakṣmī</s>], the experience of indulgence through the taking of <s>sīdhu</s> (liquor) — the enjoyment of pleasures — is for all times; they do not proceed according to the view of <s>Suratha</s>, the <s>Vaiśya</s>, and others. This is the meaning. || 30.2

children.text: * yuvatīnāṃ prāśane niyamavidhiṃ saṃpradarśayati || 30.3]
children.translated_text: * He demonstrates the restrictive rule for women's drinking: || 30.3]

body.translated_text: * [<Commentary on the <s>Kādambarīsvīkaraṇasūtramañjarī</s>>
For young women, the permission is in the company of their own beloved. // 31

children.text: * svakīyapriyasāhacaryeṇeti || 31.1
children.translated_text: * 'In the company of their own beloved' — || 31.1

children.text: * nidhuvanakāle eva svapatibhiḥ sārdhaṃ kādambarasvīkaraṇasyābhyanujñānaṃ netarāvasthāyāṃ kutaḥ upayogābhāvāt niṣphalaprayāse svīkaraṇasya vaiyarthyāpatteḥ || 31.2
children.translated_text: * Only at the time of love-making, the permission for accepting <s>kādambara</s> (liquor) is together with their own husbands, not in other circumstances. Why? Because of the absence of purpose [otherwise] — for the acceptance would be futile in a fruitless endeavor. || 31.2

children.text: * niyamavidhāv api kiṃcid viśeṣāntaram anubadhnāti || 31.3]
children.translated_text: * He adds a further distinction even within the restrictive rule: || 31.3]

body.translated_text: * [<Commentary on the <s>Kādambarīsvīkaraṇasūtramañjarī</s>>
Even there, the injunction is only during rites performed by none other [than one's husband], not elsewhere. // 32

children.text: * tatrāpi ananyajamakheṣv eveti || 32.1
children.translated_text: * 'Even there, only during rites performed by none other' — || 32.1

children.text: * ananyajena kriyamāṇeṣu makheṣv eva atyāvaśyakatvena anutarṣasvīkaraṇavidhānaṃ netaratra tadatiriktakāleṣv iti || 32.2
children.translated_text: * The injunction for accepting after-thirst [liquor] is absolutely necessary only during rites performed by none other [than one's husband], not at other times beyond those. || 32.2

children.text: * yoṣāyāḥ atra yoṣāsaṃgraheṇa upaśyāmādīnām eva saṃgrahaḥ na vibhraṃśitadvitīyāvasthānām āsyapadmena prāśanaṃ tu atyutkṛṣṭaphalaviśeṣāntaraṃ niścitya atyāvaśyakatvena prāśanam anudarśayati || 32.3]
children.translated_text: * By 'woman' (<s>yoṣā</s>) here, through the inclusion of women, only young women and the like are included, not those who have fallen from the second stage [of life]. Feeding through the lotus-mouth, however, having determined it as a distinctly superior fruit, he demonstrates the feeding as absolutely necessary: || 32.3]

body.translated_text: * [<Commentary on the <s>Kādambarīsvīkaraṇasūtramañjarī</s>>

body.text: yoṣāyāḥ āsyapadmena prāśanaṃ bhāṣāyāḥ prabodhe avyabhicaritakāraṇam // 33
body.translated_text: Feeding from the lotus-mouth of a woman is an unfailing cause for the awakening of speech (eloquence). // 33

children.text: * yoṣāyāḥ āsyapadmeneti || 33.1
children.translated_text: * 'From the lotus-mouth of a woman' — || 33.1

children.text: * yoṣāyāḥ āsyapadmena prāśane kriyamāṇe yathecchikī bhāṣāyāḥ anusphurtir bhavatīty arthaḥ || 33.2
children.translated_text: * When feeding is done from the lotus-mouth of a woman, spontaneous manifestation of speech occurs — this is the meaning. || 33.2

children.text: * anena vākyena śravaṇādivyavasāyarahite 'pi jane niṣprayāsenaiva tridaśānāṃ gīḥ svamukhāt prādurbhūyata ity arthaḥ || 33.3
children.translated_text: * By this statement [it is meant that] even in a person devoid of the discipline of listening and other [studies], the speech of the gods effortlessly manifests from one's own mouth — this is the meaning. || 33.3

children.text: * anyad apy utkṛṣṭataraṃ phalaviśeṣāntaraṃ svīkāramātreṇa saṃpradarśayati || 33.4]
children.translated_text: * He demonstrates yet another, even more exalted distinct fruit, merely through acceptance: || 33.4]

body.translated_text: * [<Commentary on the <s>Kādambarīsvīkaraṇasūtramañjarī</s>>

body.text: śyāmāyā āsyasahasrapattrād anuprāśanam aparokṣānubhavena mūlaprakṛteḥ svarūpasyānudarśanam // 34
body.translated_text: Drinking from the thousand-petaled lotus-mouth of <s>Śyāmā</s> (a dark-complexioned woman) [leads to] the direct realization of the essential nature of the primordial <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). // 34

children.text: * śyāmāyā āsyasahasrapattrād iti || 34.1
children.translated_text: * 'From the thousand-petaled lotus-mouth of <s>Śyāmā</s>' — || 34.1

children.text: * śyāmāyāḥ kamalaprasūnāt anuprāśanaṃ pratyakṣānubhavena sākṣāt mūlaprakṛteḥ svarūpānudarśane hetuḥ kāraṇam iti tayā saha saṃprāśane kriyamāṇe kṛtsnasya prapañcasya kāraṇabhūtāyāḥ mūlaprakṛteḥ sākaṃ saṃgato bhavati || 34.2
children.translated_text: * The drinking by the <s>śyāmā</s> of the lotus-bloom [wine] is the cause, i.e., the reason, for the direct vision of the true nature of <s>Mūlaprakṛti</s> (primordial nature) through immediate experience. When the drinking together with her is being performed, one becomes united with <s>Mūlaprakṛti</s>, who is the cause of the entire phenomenal world (<s>prapañca</s>). || 34.2

children.text: * yad vā tatsvarūpaṃ sākṣād avyavadhānena paśyatīty arthaḥ || 34.3
children.translated_text: * Or, one directly sees her true nature without any obstruction — this is the meaning. || 34.3

children.text: * anena vākyena sāyujyādikaṃ phalam api nirāyāsena prāpnotīty arthaḥ || 34.4
children.translated_text: * By this statement, the meaning is that one also attains the fruit of <s>sāyujya</s> (complete union with the divine) and the like without any effort. || 34.4

children.text: * ratikāle sīdhupānaṃ kartavyaṃ vidhibodhitam || 34.5
children.translated_text: * At the time of love-play, the drinking of <s>sīdhu</s> (fermented liquor) should be performed as taught by the rules. || 34.5

children.text: * tat purastāt kāmaśāstre proktaṃ krīḍānuvarṇanam || 34.6
children.translated_text: * That description of amorous play was previously stated in the <s>Kāmaśāstra</s>. || 34.6

children.text: * tat sarvaṃ tu prakartavyaṃ yoṣāyāḥ sukhalabdhaye || 34.7
children.translated_text: * All of that should be practiced for the attainment of the woman's pleasure. || 34.7

children.text: * svasyāpi sukhabodhāya apatyotpattihetave || 34.8
children.translated_text: * And for the awakening of one's own pleasure, and for the sake of the production of offspring. || 34.8

children.text: * phaladvayaṃ sa prāpnoti prajāṃ kāmasukhaṃ tathā || 34.9
children.translated_text: * He attains a twofold fruit: progeny and the pleasure of desire. || 34.9

children.text: * urvaśīlokam āpnoti antakāle tu saḥ pumān || 34.10
children.translated_text: * And at the time of death, that man attains the world of <s>Urvaśī</s>. || 34.10

children.text: * iti śrīmahārājarṣivaryeṇa purūravasā viracitaṃ kāmijanānāṃ vinodāya rativilāsāṅgabhūtaṃ kādambarasvīkaraṇasūtraṃ savyākhyānaṃ samāptim agamat || 34.11]
children.translated_text: * Thus the <s>Kādambarīsvīkaraṇasūtra</s> (Sūtra on the Consumption of Wine), which forms a limb of erotic play (<s>rativilāsa</s>), composed for the delight of amorous persons by the illustrious foremost among great royal sages, <s>Purūravas</s>, together with its commentary, has come to completion. || 34.11]

body.translated_text: * [<Commentary on the <s>Kādambarīsvīkaraṇasūtramañjarī</s>>
